perspective:
From Ethan Mohamud’s available perspective:

- Ethan knows Gary and he have been close friends since middle school and have supported each other over the years.
- Ethan noticed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep. He became concerned.
- Ethan invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat to relax and gain perspective. He told Gary that his health mattered, that he hated seeing Gary like this, and that the retreat might help. Gary initially declined, saying there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected there was more to Gary’s overworking than professional obligations.
- Ethan confronted Gary, saying they had been friends since middle school, that Gary could tell him anything, and that he was there to help, not judge. Gary replied that it was complicated and that he hadn’t wanted to burden Ethan.
- After the confrontation, Gary opened up to Ethan about pressures from managing a new department and personal challenges. Ethan felt relief and empathy. Ethan suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary and discussed his progress and remaining challenges. Ethan saw Gary making efforts to change and felt hopeful and proud. Ethan told Gary he was proud and available whenever Gary needed to talk. Gary said things were better, he was less overwhelmed thanks to Ethan’s help, and he had time for a movie the previous weekend.
- After a year, Ethan saw Gary managing on his own. Ethan felt satisfied and happy for Gary. He decided to step back but told Gary he was always just a call away, knew Gary had this, and should keep up the great work. Gary thanked him, said he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and felt more in control.

Ethan does not have access to any private thoughts, hidden events, or details of Gary’s struggles beyond what Gary said or showed to him.
